# ECN-2026-028 Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

Related documents: MM-P2-L2-HT02, MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, SOP-P2-L2-01

Reason for change
This engineering change notice is issued to document and formalize an adjustment to the quench delay control logic for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02). Field incident reports and subsequent investigation identified inconsistent quench initiation during parts handling transitions, producing variability in hardness outcomes and increasing rework rates on affected ring geometries. Root cause analysis determined the control sequence allowed the quench actuator to engage before the part verified position and after a variable operator hold, producing an inconsistent hold-to-quench interval.

Corrective action requires a definitive, measurable limit on the allowable delay between the verified part ready state and initiation of the quench operation in the furnace control program. The new control parameter will reduce process variability, align equipment behavior with metallurgical expectations, and reduce rework and scrap.

The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds.

Affected items
- Control program parameter on EQ-P2-L2-HT02 that governs delay from part ready confirmation to quench initiation.
- Associated human-machine interface screens and operator guidance that reference the previous unspecified delay behavior.
- Maintenance checklists and preventive maintenance tasks that reference quench timing in MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.
- Standard operating procedure steps in SOP-P2-L2-01 that describe the quench sequence and operator confirmations.

Affected stakeholders: production operators for line P2-L2, furnace maintenance technicians, process engineering, quality assurance, and metallurgical engineering. The change applies to in-process lots currently staged for processing in EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and to all future production until superseded by another controlled change.

Implementation
Scope
Implement the updated quench delay parameter in the PLC and furnace controller for EQ-P2-L2-HT02. Update operator interface text to display current measured delay and an alert when delay approaches the limit. Revise maintenance and SOP documentation to reference the new maximum delay requirement and to provide steps for verification and corrective action.

Steps
- Modify controller parameter: set the quench delay limit in the control program to the value specified above. Ensure limit is enforced as a hard constraint so that quench initiation is inhibited if the delay exceeds the limit until manual override is authorized and logged.
- Update HMI: add a visible indicator showing the real-time measured delay for each cycle and a status flag that transitions to alarm state when the measured delay reaches a threshold indicative of imminent violation.
- Update MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1: add a procedural check entry to verify the quench delay parameter and HMI indicator during functional checks. Reference the new limit explicitly in the maintenance steps so that calibrations and diagnostic tests validate the control logic.
- Update SOP-P2-L2-01: revise the operator sequencing description to include the requirement to observe the HMI delay indicator and to follow the documented steps if the indicator reports a delay approaching or exceeding the allowed maximum. Include guidance on permissible use of documented override procedures and subsequent verification steps.
- Commissioning and validation: conduct a controlled validation run sequence to demonstrate that the controller enforces the quench delay limit under typical loading and handling conditions. Record measured delay values and corresponding part hardness or process monitor outputs as evidence of compliant operation.
- Training: deliver an operator and maintenance briefing covering the change rationale, how to read the HMI delay indicator, the required actions when an alarm occurs, and reporting expectations. Training records will be retained in accordance with plant practice.

Examples and rationale
Example scenarios are provided to clarify expected behavior:
- Where a normal pick-and-place cycle results in timely verification of part readiness, measured delay should remain well below the limit. The controller permits automatic quench initiation and the batch proceeds without intervention.
- If a handling anomaly or test hold causes delay near the allowable maximum, the HMI indicator will show the approaching limit and the operator will be required to follow the procedural steps in SOP-P2-L2-01, including pausing further cycles and notifying maintenance if the condition repeats.
- If the delay exceeds the limit, the controller will inhibit automatic quench initiation. The operator will follow documented override and verification steps, and a maintenance ticket will be generated to investigate mechanical or sensor faults.

Records to keep
Maintain records of:
- Controller configuration change log for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 showing the parameter update and the implementing engineer.
- Commissioning validation records including measured delay traces and companion process data that demonstrate compliance to the maximum delay requirement.
- HMI alarm logs and any manual override entries related to quench delay events.
- Updated maintenance checklists and signoffs in MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 showing completed verification steps.
- Operator training attendance and acknowledgement that SOP-P2-L2-01 revisions were reviewed.

Approvals
Approval of this change requires signoff from process engineering, maintenance management, operations management for line P2-L2, and quality assurance. Upon approval, the change will be implemented and the related documents MM-P2-L2-HT02, MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, and SOP-P2-L2-01 will be revision-controlled to reflect the required updates.
